title: VPC traffic policy and SIEM mapping guide
content:
Purpose:
This guide consolidates operational patterns for private-deploy VPC/network hardening, how to map firewall + mTLS events into our audit log schema, and a lightweight evidence automation pipeline for SIEM ingestion. Intended audience: infra engineers, security owners for Private deployments, SREs, and compliance reviewers.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to Private (VPC) deployments managed by Redwood Private or customers running the Redwood runtime inside their VPCs.
- Focus on network-level controls (VPC subnet design, egress/ingress controls, firewall policies, mTLS enforcement) plus the downstream telemetry mapping and export to SIEM (Splunk/ELK/Datadog).
- Assumes existing KMS-backed certs and a PKI used for mTLS; we describe rotation and audit hooks but not PKI onboarding steps.

High-level pattern summary:
1) Network zones: management, control-plane, inference, telemetry
   - management (nat/ops): restricted CIDR ranges for admin consoles and bastion access (e.g., 10.100.0.0/24)
   - control-plane: hosts the Redwood control-plane components (config API, rollouts, model registry). Only accepts TLS from inference plane in allowed subnets.
   - inference plane: model servers, GPU nodes. Accepts mTLS from customer-facing routes and control-plane.
   - telemetry: egress-only endpoints for metrics, traces, and log shipping to SIEM collectors.

Example VPC layout (CIDR placeholders):
- VPC: 10.100.0.0/16
  - management: 10.100.0.0/24
  - control-plane: 10.100.1.0/24
  - inference-private: 10.100.2.0/22
  - telemetry-egress: 10.100.16.0/28 (collector NAT)

Firewall policy (high level rules):
- Block-by-default posture. Only allow explicit flows:
  - management -> control-plane: TCP/443 from 10.100.0.0/24 -> 10.100.1.0/24 (for admin UI and API)
  - control-plane -> inference: TCP/443 + TCP/8060 (runtime heartbeat/proxy) from 10.100.1.0/24 -> 10.100.2.0/22
  - inference -> telemetry: TLS to collector IP(s) on TCP/443 and TCP/6514 (syslog)
  - customer-ingress -> inference: mTLS enforced on TCP/443; source IPs typically managed by cloud LB and ACLs
  - no inbound SSH to inference nodes; debug via bastion in management zone with recorded session auditing

Rule examples (CIDR/APPLICATION):
- ALLOW: 10.100.0.0/24 -> 10.100.1.0/24 TCP/443 (admin-api)
- ALLOW: 10.100.1.0/24 -> 10.100.2.0/22 TCP/443, TCP/8060 (runtime)
- ALLOW: 10.100.2.0/22 -> 10.100.16.0/28 TCP/443 (metrics/traces/log-forwarder)
- DENY: 0.0.0.0/0 -> 10.100.2.0/22 TCP/22 (block SSH)

mTLS enforcement pattern:
- All inter-zone service-to-service traffic authenticates with mTLS using short-lived certs (recommended <= 24h TTL for leaf certs).
- Control-plane issues signed leaf certs via internal CA; inference nodes request certs during boot and rotate via a sidecar controller.
- TLS ciphers: TLS1.2+ with AEAD suites; require ECDHE and strong KDFs per cloud provider best practices.
- Failure modes: if mTLS validation fails, connections are rejected and an audit log event is emitted (see audit schema).

Certificate rotation & evidence hooks:
- Rotation trigger events: scheduled rotation (cron), CA rotation, node reprovision.
- Evidence to capture automatically:
  - cert thumbprint, subject, issuer, notBefore, notAfter (timestamped)
  - rotation trigger id (cron job id or Jira/Runbook id)
  - node id and ephemeral key fingerprint
  - PKI operation logs (CA issue/revoke responses)
- Store rotation artifacts in the evidence bucket with immutability tags and link them in the audit event.

RBAC v2 mapping to network zones (quick reference):
- RBAC role: "infra-admin" -> network permitted: management zone controls, create/update firewall rules, view audit events; actions always require 2FA and originate from management CIDR.
- RBAC role: "deploy-svc" -> can push config to control-plane and request certs; network actions limited to control-plane API endpoints.
- RBAC role: "observability" -> can read telemetry endpoints and query SIEM; cannot update firewall or PKI.
- Enforcement: network ACL rules are tied to role-bound tags on ephemeral admin sessions; when a session is granted, the bastion will open temporary ACL entries, each issuance emits an audit event with session_id and requestor.

Audit log schema (canonical fields) - purpose: ensure uniform SIEM parsing and evidence links. The schema below is the recommended minimum for network/mTLS/firewall events.
- timestamp: RFC3339 UTC
- event_id: UUID
- event_type: string (e.g., "network.allow","network.deny","mtls.failure","cert.rotate","firewall.change","bastion.session")
- source_ip: string (cidr single IP)
- source_identity: string (role/session/user id if available)
- dest_ip: string
- dest_port: string or int
- proto: string (tcp/udp)
- action: string (allow/deny/reject)
- policy_id: string (internal firewall rule id)
- reason: short text (automated reason or human-entered note)
- severity: string (info/warn/critical)
- evidence_links: list (comma-separated) of signed URLs or artifact ids
- raw_event: base64 or compressed blob of the original firewall/iptables message for forensic replay

Audit log schema (example JSON event string - escaped for embedding):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-19T15:23:10Z",
  "event_id": "d3b07384-df4a-4a5b-9f1b-2a2afc6a1c1a",
  "event_type": "mtls.failure",
  "source_ip": "203.0.113.45",
  "source_identity": "deploy-svc:session-2245",
  "dest_ip": "10.100.1.42",
  "dest_port": 443,
  "proto": "tcp",
  "action": "reject",
  "policy_id": "fw-ctrlplane-013",
  "reason": "client cert expired",
  "severity": "warn",
  "evidence_links": "s3://evidence.prod/redwood/private-deploys/certs/rotate/2026-02-19/session-2245.zip",
  "raw_event": "H4sIAAAAA...base64compressed..."
}

SIEM export mapping notes (Splunk/ELK):
- Ingest pipeline should normalize the canonical fields above into top-level SIEM fields. When shipping via Fluentd/Vector, use the following mapping rules:
  - timestamp -> @timestamp
  - event_type -> event.action
  - source_identity -> user.name
  - policy_id -> network.policy.id
  - evidence_links -> event.evidence
- Recommended JSON tag: add "redwood.private_deploy": true to all exported docs for quick filtering.
- Enrichment: on ingest, call internal asset service to resolve dest_ip -> node_id, node_role; add node.risk_score and owner.team. Ensure enrichment runs asynchronously and does not block ingestion.

Evidence automation pipeline (lightweight runbook):
1) Trigger collection: event triggers (mtls.failure, firewall.change, bastion.session start/stop) are emitted into the local log bus.
2) Collector service picks up event -> calls the evidence orchestrator with event_id and type.
3) Orchestrator runs evidence actions based on a policy:
   - mtls.failure -> capture cert chain, recent TLS handshake logs, system journal (last 1h), and copy sidecar logs.
   - firewall.change -> snapshot current firewall config, diff vs last committed, store diff and annotate with user.id and PR/CL id.
   - bastion.session -> record session transcript and upload to immutable evidence store.
4) Orchestrator writes a signed manifest to the evidence store and creates an audit event linking the manifest id.
5) SIEM ingestor pulls audit events and the manifest link, attaches manifest metadata (size, sha256, signed_by) and adds a retention tag for compliance (e.g., 7 years for regulated customers).

Retention & tamper-evidence:
- Evidence store is S3 or object-store with versioning + object lock. Manifests are signed with an HSM-backed key.
- Maintain a signed ledger (append-only) of evidence manifest ids; ledger entries are also exported daily into SIEM as a special event type: evidence.ledger.append.

Alerting & playbooks (examples):
- Alert: repeated mtls.failure from same source within 10 minutes -> Severity: high. Playbook: block source IP at firewall, create an incident in PagerDuty, notify infra-admin, escalate to SRE oncall if >3 failures in 5 minutes.
- Alert: firewall.change without associated RBAC session token or PR -> Severity: critical. Playbook: trigger automated rollback and quarantine rule, require manual review.

Operational checklists (pre-deployment):
- Verify VPC zone CIDRs do not overlap with customer-managed ranges.
- Enforce deny-by-default firewall baseline.
- Confirm mTLS CA is provisioned and test cert issuance/rotation via canary node.
- Validate audit log stream to SIEM (sample event ingestion + enrichment).
- Confirm evidence store lifecycle and object-lock policies are in place.

Incident checklist (triage):
- Capture event_id and corresponding evidence manifest id immediately.
- Pull recent cert rotation logs and sidecar TLS logs.
- If geo/source unusual, escalate and block IPs at cloud-provider ACLs.
- Document rollback actions with policy_id and a reason string.

Diagram notes (quick ASCII layout for architecture diagrams):
  [Admin/Bastion - 10.100.0.0/24]--(443)->[Control-plane - 10.100.1.0/24]--(mTLS)->[Inference - 10.100.2.0/22]
                                  |
                                  +--(443)->[Telemetry Collector - 10.100.16.0/28]---> SIEM

- For design diagrams use: left=management, center=control-plane, right=inference, bottom=telemetry. Annotate arrows with enforced policies (mTLS=yes, ports, RBAC tokens required).

Appendix A: small troubleshooting checklist (fast wins):
- Confirm system time drift < 3s between nodes (mTLS cert validation sensitive to clock skew).
- Check SNI and ALPN presence on failing TLS handshakes.
- Validate that firewall rules have correct policy_id tags; if missing, SIEM correlation will fail.

Appendix B: sample automation snippets (pseudo commands):
- Capture evidence manifest: 
  runbook-cli evidence capture --event d3b07384-df4a-4a5b-9f1b-2a2afc6a1c1a --artifacts cert-chain,journal,sidecar-logs --store s3://evidence.prod

- Quick SIEM search (Splunk):
  index=redwood_priv event.action=mtls.failure | stats count by source_ip, dest_ip, reason

Closing notes and next steps:
- Action items: automate enrichment for dest_ip->node.owner and include owner.contact in SIEM alerts (owner.team).
- Suggested follow-up: schedule a tabletop for RBAC+Network change scenarios (2hr) and test the evidence automation end-to-end in a staging VPC.

Document owner: Ava Chen (eng-private-deployments). Please review and add notes in the document comments or link PRs to JIRA-PLT-789 for proposed automation changes.
